raw_record.question_stem: Which choice best states what the study implies about vacant lots?
raw_record.passage: Urban planners once treated vacant lots as problems to be cleared. In several cities, however, community groups have turned these spaces into gardens. A study of twelve such gardens found that residents visited them more often when plots included benches and shaded paths. The findings suggest that design, rather than the mere presence of plants, determines whether a vacant lot becomes a shared neighborhood space.

answer_choices.choice_text: Vacant lots should always be cleared before residents can use them.
Residents visit gardens only when the gardens contain a large number of plants.
Garden design features can influence whether residents use vacant lots.
Community gardens are less useful than other forms of public space.
